title: Ice Cream 1.5L

drivers.name: Competitor opening
drivers.evidence: New competitor across the street; no prior data, but price increase to $6.56 in past week (2026-09-28) saw sales drop to x0.54 vs baseline. Competitor entry likely reduces demand, especially with price increase. Evidence is weak but directional.

drivers.name: Price increase (+2.3%)
drivers.evidence: Same price point in 2026-09-28 saw sales at x0.54 vs baseline. No prior promotions at this price. Noise-adjusted effect of past promotions is x1.25, but no lift observed at this price, suggesting demand is price-sensitive.

adjustment.analysis: No events or promotions are scheduled. The price increase to $6.56 (+2.3%) is modest and not deep enough to trigger a strong lift. Past promotions show a noise-adjusted median lift of x1.25, but none at this price point. The competitor opening across the street introduces a downside risk. Historical data shows no price sensitivity above x1.0 at this level, and the recent week with same price (2026-09-28) sold 24 units (x0.54 vs baseline), suggesting price sensitivity. The competitor entry is a new risk with no prior data. Adjust down slightly. No evidence of seasonal or holiday lift. Final adjustment shrinks toward 1.0 due to thin evidence.

brief:
PRODUCT: Ice Cream 1.5L | category Frozen | Store #12 (Austin, TX)
TARGET WEEK: 2026-11-16 to 2026-11-22 (6 weeks after the last week with sales data)

KNOWN PLAN FOR THE TARGET WEEK:
  events: none
  shelf price: 6.56 (+2.3% vs regular price 6.41)
  planner notes: A competitor opens a store across the street this week

STATISTICAL BASELINE (exponential smoothing of recent sales; it ignores events, promotions and prices):
  median 44.3 | 5%-95%: 13.0 - 73.8 | 10%-90%: 21.3 - 69.6

In the evidence below, 'vs baseline' = actual units / what this same baseline predicted for that week.
It is the multiplier that would have been right, so it maps directly onto median_multiplier.
This product's ordinary weeks already swing about +/-36% around the baseline, so a past effect smaller than that, seen only a few times, is mostly noise. The
'noise-adjusted estimate' is the effect shrunk toward x1.0 for that noise and the number of sightings.
